chief_complaint: finger locked in palm, failing steroid injections
hpi_details: A 77-year-old man has chronic painful catching and locking of a finger in flexion despite prior corticosteroid injections, limiting daily hand use.
ideas: thinks it might be related to trigger_finger_surgery
concerns: worried about potential complications and long term recovery
expectations: wants complete diagnostic evaluation and treatment plan

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Trigger Finger release is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.
Standard management emphasizes Plan for Trigger Finger release: Refer for outpatient surgical trigger finger release, adapted to individual patient risk factors and clinical severity.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: finger locked in palm, failing steroid injections
Key HPI features: Chronic painful catching and locking persists despite corticosteroid injections and limits hand use.
Objective/Exam findings: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Trigger Finger release.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Trigger Finger release.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Soft tissue infection without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Missing acute flexor tenosynovitis or traumatic neurovascular injury before treating as routine trigger finger.
management_principles: Plan for Trigger Finger release: Refer for outpatient surgical trigger finger release
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

reference_soap.objective: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Trigger Finger release.
reference_soap.assessment: Trigger finger (stenosing flexor tenosynovitis) refractory to corticosteroid injections.

teaching.one_liner: Plastic and reconstructive surgical case presenting with finger locked in palm, failing steroid injections.
differentials: Flexor tendon nodule from rheumatoid arthritis
red_flags: Acute severe finger pain with fusiform swelling, warmth, fever, or pain on passive extension requiring urgent assessment for flexor tenosynovitis
Acute trauma, deformity, neurovascular change, or inability to actively extend after injury requiring urgent hand evaluation

must_ask.say: How long has your finger been locking, and does it happen with every movement?
Do you feel pain or a clicking sensation when you bend or straighten the finger?
How many steroid injections have you had, and did they help at all?
Do you have diabetes or any other conditions that affect your hands?
How does the locking affect your ability to do daily tasks or work?
